BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                    )
 EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR                           )
 REVISION OF ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES                  )   Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317                      )


ORDER ON EPE’S PROPOSED SECOND NOTICE AND SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGN

       THIS MATTER comes before the Hearing Examiners upon El Paso Electric Company’s

(“EPE”) Notice of Compliance Filing of Proposed Form of Website Notice (“EPE’s Compliance

Filing”), and The City of Las Cruces’ (“CLC”) Comments on El Paso Electric Company’s

Proposed Second Notice to EPE Customers and Social Media Campaign (“CLC’s Comments”).

Being duly informed, the Hearing Examiners FIND and CONCLUDE:

       1.       On August 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued an Order Establishing

Revised Procedural Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions (“August 27th Order”), in

which the Hearing Examiners ordered EPE to file a proposed form of website notice for EPE’s

Amended Application, and to describe the manner in which EPE will conduct a social media

campaign for that notice, including a description of how the social media campaign will connect

customers to the form of notice that will be made available on EPE’s website. The Hearing

Examiners also ordered that on or before September 10, 2026, parties were permitted to file

comments on EPE’s proposed form of website notice and EPE’s filed plan for its social media

campaign. Further, the Hearing Examiners committed to confirming and/or defining the final form

of website notice, and social media campaign, on or before September 15, 2026.

       2.       On September 3, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Compliance Filing.

       3.       On September 10, 2026, CLC filed CLC’s Comments, which identified several

concerns with respect to EPE’s Compliance Filing.
            BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on EPE’s Proposed Second Notice                Docket No. 25-00082-UT


         4.        EPE’s Compliance Filing does not include a complete table of the rates, for all

rate classes, that EPE has proposed in its Amended Application, in the same format as the rate

table that is accessible through the QR Code in the Notice to EPE Customers initially provided to

ratepayers,     and    which     is    currently    accessible    here:   https://www.prc.nm.gov/wp-

content/uploads/2026/04/Notice-B-QR-Tables.pdf. As noted by CLC, the initial Notice provided

a link to “detailed information about current and proposed rate components for all classes of

service that EPE provides in New Mexico, while the (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers

provides just a few figures for Standard Residential Service under Rate No. 1.” 1

         5.        The Amended Application requests Commission determinations for all rate

classes, and it is therefore reasonable that a Second Notice to EPE Customers provide access to

information for all rate classes.

         6.        Additionally, EPE’s (Proposed) Second Notice to EPE Customers, included in

EPE’s Compliance Filing, states that EPE “intends to conduct a paid social media campaign related

to the [Amended] Application on Meta platforms, Facebook and Instagram, beginning September

15, 2026, for an anticipated duration of approximately one week,” and that “[t]he advertisement

will provide a direct link to the Amended Application Notice posted on EPE’s website, ….”

         7.        EPE’s Compliance Filing does not, however, identify specific text that will be

used to communicate with users of the Meta platforms, nor an explanation of the amount of

communications that will be disseminated during the week-long social media campaign. The

Hearing Examiners therefore do not have sufficient information to confirm or define EPE’s filed

plan for its social media campaign.



   1
       CLC’s Comments (September 10, 2026) ¶ 6. (Emphasis in original).


                                                   -2-
            BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on EPE’s Proposed Second Notice                Docket No. 25-00082-UT


         8.       Hence, the Hearing Examiners find it necessary to delay their issuance of an order

confirming and/or defining the final form of website notice and EPE’s filed plan for its social

media campaign. The Hearing Examiners instead require that further information be filed by EPE. 2


   IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

         A.       By September 18, 2026:

                   1.   EPE shall file with the Commission a complete table of rates, and a

                   comparison of present and proposed rates for each customer class as

                   requested in the Amended Application, in the same format as the

                   information that is provided in the “Continuation Notice to EPE

                   Customers” available here:

                   https://www.prc.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Notice-B-QR-

                   Tables.pdf

                   2.   EPE shall include with its filing a description of the actual text that

                   the “advertisement” will utilize to communicate with the users of the

                   Meta platforms and a more robust explanation of the amount of

                   communications that will be disseminated in the social media campaign.

         B.       After EPE provides the information required by this Order, the Hearing

Examiners will proceed to issue an order that defines the Form of Website Notice and

Social Media Campaign.




   2
       See 1.2.2.29(C)(9) NMAC
